reason:
The theorem is correct as an identity, and it holds up under the real conditions. The headline consequence does not follow, and the decision it changes is tiny.

What holds:
(1) Lemma 1, Lemma 2 and the Cauchy-Schwarz bound only need three things: K32 + K96 ~ Bin(m, r), the counts independent of the steered/round-4 continuations given the prefix, and the final test run on the same prefixes. Question clustering does not break this, and neither does a non-Beta risk law. Prefix-level dose-response heterogeneity beyond r does not break it either, provided F_0 is taken as the full latent prefix state rather than r.
(2) The §7.11 h_3 are chosen by y_2 text and by the e_2 of the h_2 trajectory, never by their own 32 `sel` counts. So K32 is unselected given r, as A0 needs.
(3) I re-ran the nested MC with the production function in question-clustered worlds: logit-normal risks, 50 questions × 4 prefixes, ICC 0, 0.7 and 0.9, 800 outer × 200 inner, posterior drawn exactly per question by importance resampling. The σ_δ 95% UCL for REJECT was 0.0000 / 0.0047 / 0.0052 under HC1 and 0.0023 / 0.0065 / 0.0057 under CR1, about the same as the Beta cells. A realistic adoption rule (PD32) gave reuse − fresh of +0.0004 to +0.0011 (SE about 0.0009). In route C's own runs, the realistic rule "adopt128 = not certify32" (P(D) about 0.9) gives |reuse − fresh| ≤ 0.001. Reuse really is harmless for size in every world tested.

What does not follow:
(a) "Admissible for the SIZE target" mixes up the reuse increment with the size target. The two-stage size is P(R) + selection term + reuse term. The claim spends the whole ±0.02 tolerance on the reuse term alone. In the half-variance world the one-stage size is already 0.022, outside [0.03, 0.07], whether counts are reused or fresh. In my clustered worlds the total conditional-size sd (selection + reuse) has a UCL of 0.0068–0.0078, which allows deviations of 0.020–0.023 at P(D) = 0.1. Clustering inflates the selection term, which is present under fresh counts too. Under CR1 at ICC 0.7, the reuse term alone is 0.0196 at P(D) = 0.1, right at the tolerance edge.
(b) "For every rule with P(adopt) ≥ 0.1 ... ≤ 0.019 / 0.014" is a guarantee only for the named Beta worlds. Route C's own Remark (iv) says σ_δ is not identified from the pilot. The r4 obstacle asks for a statement over the whole set of risk laws compatible with the pilot counts, and the claim explicitly does not cover that set. P(D) is also a property of the unknown world, so the condition P(D) ≥ 0.1 cannot be checked.
(c) The r4 decision criterion covers false-positive rate AND interval width. The claim protects neither width nor non-PD (σ_δ up to 0.085). In the half-variance world, P(width ≤ 0.15) = 0.27 and non-PD = 12% at m = 128 one-stage, so the 128 decision there is settled by one-stage operating characteristics, not by reuse versus fresh. At the 128 stage the PD flag and the width proxy can be computed from the 128 counts alone (route C's F1), so the conditional-evaluation advice adds little.
(d) The decision changed is negligible. The plan does not currently require fresh regressor continuations: §7.2b D4 already allows `sel`-only h_3 continuations for matching and stratification, and §7.11 already uses r̂^sel as the regressor. Running fresh instead of reusing costs 200 × 32 × about 600 tok ≈ 3.8e6 vLLM tokens, about 0.01 GPU-day against roughly 19 A100-days of HF budget.

Preconditions the plan would have to state:
- The production `endpoint_contrast_poly_cs` takes one scalar m. If continuation counts differ across prefixes (failed generations), neither reuse nor fresh is supported as written.
- No per-prefix screening on r̂(h_3) from the reused 32 (archive R5 caveat). Even dropping 0/32 prefixes would bias U_j(K32 + K96) given selection, and the theorem would no longer apply.
- If the adoption rule also uses the 64 h_2 bank counts, it falls outside σ(t, K32). The identity still generalizes if F_0 is the latent prefix state, but no constants were computed for that case.
fix:
Restate the consequence as a statement about reuse versus fresh, not about meeting the size target. Suggested wording: "Under A0, with the 200 h_3 unscreened on their own sel counts and a common m, reusing the 32 sel counts changes the conditional two-stage size relative to fresh counts by at most σ_δ·sqrt((1−π)/π). In the Beta cells and in question-clustered logit-normal checks, σ_δ ≤ 0.0065 (HC1/CR1). For the realistic adoption rule (π ≈ 0.9) the change is ≤ 0.001. Meeting the size target still depends on the one-stage size at 128 and the selection term over the set of compatible risk laws (routes A/B). Width and non-PD must be judged one-stage at 128."
Also:
- Drop "the user does not need to spend 32 extra draws" as a decision driver. Note instead that fresh counts cost ≈3.8e6 vLLM tokens (≈0.01 GPU-day), remove the reuse question entirely, and may be preferred for simplicity.
- Add to the plan the requirements of a common m and no per-prefix r̂ screening.
- Report the combined selection + reuse sd (Var P(R|G32)), not σ_δ alone, next to the ±0.02 tolerance.
strongest_attack_tried: I re-ran the production nested Monte Carlo in worlds outside the claim's scope: question-clustered, non-Beta risks (logit-normal, ICC 0 / 0.7 / 0.9, 50 questions × 4 prefixes, 2 per type), with the exact joint posterior per question drawn by importance resampling (20,000 prior draws, median ESS 1,500–1,800). Each world ran 800 outer × 200 inner, with HC1 and CR1, and the realistic rule PD32 was evaluated alongside. The point was to test whether σ_δ and the tolerance claim carry over to the real pipeline. Separately, I checked each precondition against plan §5.5, §7.2b, §7.11 and §7.13, the production function's scalar-m signature, and the r4 obstacle's criterion (false-positive rate AND width, quantified over the compatible risk laws).
